newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Oasis may sue over Internet copyright.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Oasis may sue over Internet copyright.

text.p: The management of leading British pop group Oasis is threatening legal action for breach of copyright against hundreds of unofficial Internet sites dedicated to the band, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said the Oasis initiative was a first for the music industry but formed part of a general clampdown against intellectual copyright infringements on the Internet.

"In its warning to unauthorised Oasis web sites, Ignition Management says it is unlawful to use copyrighted photographs, video clips, song lyrics and sound samples without permission, and has given them 30 days to erase illegal material," the Financial Times said.

The newspaper said many unofficial sites for pop acts were run by fans who did not benefit commercially but "others have been commandeered by bootleggers (pirates) to sell counterfeit CDs and cassettes, often of dubious quality".

It quoted Sara John, legal counsultant to the British Phonographic Industry which represents the country's record companies, as saying the issue of policing the Internet was "a very difficult one because it is virtually impossible to distinguish genuine fan sites from the out-and-out rogues".
